nodes.name: Intake Form
nodes.notes: STAGE: input/intake. A human starts one analysis run by submitting this form. No file content is embedded in the workflow -- paths are supplied at submission time, resolved on the Windows-host Python service relative to its project root (see docs/n8n-setup.md).

parameters.formDescription: Paths are resolved by the Python HTTP service on the Windows host, relative to its project root (see setup docs). This step only runs analysis -- it never creates a GitHub issue.

nodes.name: Build Analyze Request
nodes.notes: Builds the JSON body for POST /analyze on the Windows-host HTTP service (Stage 13 orchestrator, exposed via api.py). No analysis logic lives here -- it only reshapes the form inputs into the AnalyzeRequest schema (splits the comma-separated context-files field into an array).

nodes.name: Run Analysis (HTTP)
nodes.notes: STAGE: analysis invocation. Calls POST /analyze on the small Product Feedback Agent HTTP service running on the Windows host (src/product_feedback_agent/api.py), which delegates directly to the reusable Stage 13 orchestrator.run_analysis (analyst -> deterministic validator -> critic -> optional single revision). No core product logic is duplicated in n8n. host.docker.internal lets this Docker-hosted n8n instance reach the Windows-host service -- see docs/n8n-setup.md. Replaces the Stage 15 Execute Command node, which failed on live import because n8n's Execute Command node was not installed on the target instance, and would in any case have run inside the n8n container rather than the Windows host's .venv.

nodes.name: Parse Orchestration Result
nodes.notes: The HTTP Request node already throws on a non-2xx /analyze response (default behavior), so this is a defensive re-check plus wrapping the OrchestrationResult under an `orchestrationResult` key for the downstream nodes.

nodes.name: Render Review Summary
nodes.notes: STAGE: structured opportunity display. Renders exactly the 3 opportunities, their deterministic scores, evidence counts, and unresolved validation issues -- nothing here re-scores or re-decides anything.

nodes.name: Human Review & Approval
nodes.notes: STAGE: explicit human approval boundary. This is the ONLY step that can authorize a GitHub write. Approval is never inferred -- the human must pick 'approve' AND name one opportunity_id AND the target repo; picking 'reject' (or any other value) is treated as reject by the Approval Gate below regardless of the other two fields. Live finding (2026-09-07): this node imported with Page Type = Form Ending instead of Next Form Page, so it is now defined with operation="page" and defineForm="json" (the installed Form node's JSON-defined form mode) instead of the UI 'Using Fields Below' builder.

nodes.name: Approval Gate
nodes.notes: STAGE: approve/reject branch. Only the exact string 'approve' from the human review form continues to the GitHub-action branch. Everything else (including 'reject', blank, or malformed input) goes to the no-action branch. Deterministic validation is never bypassed here -- it already ran, unconditionally, before this gate.

nodes.name: Build GitHub Issue Request
nodes.notes: Approved path only. Builds the JSON body for POST /github/issues, carrying the ORIGINAL orchestration result (not a re-derived or n8n-edited version) plus approved=true, dry_run=false, and an allow-list containing ONLY the human-supplied repo. No core GitHub logic is duplicated here -- this only shapes the request the Windows-host HTTP service (api.py) forwards, unmodified, to the existing Stage 14 create_opportunity_issue.

nodes.name: Create GitHub Issue (Approved)
nodes.notes: STAGE: GitHub action, approved path only. This node is unreachable unless Approval Gate matched 'approve' with a named opportunity_id and repo. Calls POST /github/issues on the Windows-host HTTP service, which delegates directly to the existing, unmodified Stage 14 create_opportunity_issue -- that function independently re-checks approved/dry-run/allow-list/duplicate before ever calling GitHub, so this node cannot bypass those guards. Replaces the Stage 15 Execute Command node for the same reason as 'Run Analysis (HTTP)' above.

nodes.name: Parse GitHub Action Result
nodes.notes: The HTTP Request node already throws on a non-2xx /github/issues response (default behavior); this wraps the IssueActionResult under an `actionResult` key for the downstream Set node.

nodes.name: Approved Summary
nodes.notes: status will be 'created', 'refused_duplicate', 'refused_unsupported_repo', or 'refused_not_approved' -- inspect this before assuming an issue was actually filed.

nodes.name: No Action (Rejected)
nodes.notes: STAGE: rejected/no-action path. Reached whenever the human did not type 'approve' with both an opportunity_id and a repo. Intentionally connects to nothing further -- no GitHub node exists on this branch, so no mutation is structurally possible from here.
